options.title: Protect reserve monitored beds
options.description: Review and adjust policies to ensure reserve monitored beds are protected for acute arrivals, especially during periods of high bed occupancy.
options.local_fit: Policy review aligns with the observed pattern of delayed access to monitored beds due to high bed occupancy and slow physician response. This option directly addresses the gap between policy and practice.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If successful, this option may reduce pressure on nurses managing high bed occupancy, but it could shift the burden to physicians if they face increased demand for acute care. Additionally, it may impact the overall bed capacity and patient flow.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the number of available reserve monitored beds and track the success rate of acute arrivals accessing these beds promptly. Measure any changes in bed occupancy and physician response times.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the policy adjustment fails to improve access to monitored beds or if it leads to unintended consequences, such as increased wait times in other areas.

options.title: Match rooming pace to capacity
options.description: Implement a process to match the pace of rooming patients to the capacity of available physicians, especially during periods of high bed occupancy.
options.local_fit: This option addresses the observed pattern of delayed access to physicians due to slow response times, which may be influenced by the pace of rooming patients. It aims to improve efficiency and reduce wait times.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If effective, this option may reduce pressure on physicians by ensuring a more balanced workload. However, it could shift pressure to nurses if rooming processes become more complex or time-consuming.
options.how_we_would_know: Measure the impact on physician response times and patient wait times after implementing the process adjustment. Track any changes in bed occupancy and nurse workload.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the process adjustment fails to improve response times or if it leads to increased wait times or complications in rooming processes.

options.title: Communicate expected waits
options.description: Monitor and analyze the impact of communicating expected wait times to patients after rooming, especially during periods of high bed occupancy and slow physician response.
options.local_fit: This option aims to address patient frustration and improve the quality of care by providing transparency about wait times. It may help manage patient expectations and reduce complaints.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If effective, this option may reduce pressure on nurses and physicians by improving patient satisfaction. However, it could shift pressure to the communication process if not implemented effectively.
options.how_we_would_know: Track patient feedback and complaint rates related to wait times after implementing the communication strategy. Measure any changes in patient satisfaction and nurse/physician workload.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the communication strategy fails to improve patient satisfaction or if it leads to increased complaints or negative feedback.

recommendation.rationale: Although all options are supported by evidence, we recommend "Communicate expected waits" as the leading option due to its potential to improve patient satisfaction and reduce complaints, which are key aspects of quality care. Additionally, this option has the least potential to shift pressure to other roles, making it a more balanced approach.
recommendation.would_change_if: If evidence suggests that patient communication strategies are less effective or if new data shows a significant impact on nurse or physician workload, we would reconsider the leading option.

suggested_reviewers.why: Nursing leadership can provide insights into the local context, bed occupancy challenges, and the potential impact of policy adjustments on nursing practices.
Physicians can offer perspectives on the feasibility and potential impact of policy and process adjustments on their workload and response times.
